full_judgment:
10. Mr. R. Huq, the learned Advocate for the applicant firm has placed before us a decision of the Indian Supreme Court, viz. the case of the Commissioner of Income Tax, West Bengal Vs. A.W.F. Figgies and Company and others reported in A.I.R. 1953 (S.C.) 455 same case 24 I.T.R. 405 which affirmed on appeal the decision of the Calcutta High Court as reported in AIR 1952 Calcutta 677, same case, 20 I.T.R. 530. The Supreme Court of India has to construe, in that case, section 25(4) of the Income Tax Act in which it is provided that when a person carrying on any business profession or vocation on which tax was at any time charged under the provisions of the Indian Income Tax is succeeded in such capacity by another person, the change not being merely a change in the constitution of a partnership, no tax shall be payable by the first mentioned person in respect of the Income, profits and gains of the period between the end of the previous year and the date of such succession. Mahanjan J. in delivering the Judgment of the Supreme Court of India in the above mentioned case has made the following observation :— 

 (5) No application under this section for registration or renewal of registration in respect of the assessment for the year beginning on the first day of July, 1969, or for any year thereafter, shall be made unless the partnership has been registered under the Partnership Act, 1932 (XI of 1932) : 

 Provided that where such application is made for the first time and the firm is not registered under the partnership Act, 1932 (XI of 1932) or where the deed of partnership is not registered under the Registration Act, 1908 (XVI of 1908), it shall be made within a period of six months of the constitution of the firm, or before the end of the previous year in which the firm was constituted, whichever is earlier :
